Session open. Chapter 2. Approval: autopilot. Spoilers: off.

## Changed since last session
Nothing changed since the last session.

## Settings
- as of: Spring, year 300
- genre: low fantasy
- tone: grim
- difficulty: balanced
- length: standard
- pacing: balanced
- dice: GM rolls

## Voice anchor

name: log_scene

input.summary: Dawn in Rickard's command tent at the start of chapter 2. Hesse reported that the Triarch's men pulled every picket off the eastern ditch overnight and doubled the watch on the Black Wall's north face, as if they knew the company's plan; only four people knew it. Rickard touched the key at his neck, went to see the captains, and told Marro to mind the tent. Marro left anyway when the young sellswords called him to the dice house.

updates.body: Overnight at the start of chapter 2 the Triarch's men pulled every picket off the eastern ditch and doubled the watch on the Black Wall's north face (two men per merlon). The eastern ditch was the company's planned approach; only four people knew of it.
Rickard's shoulder wound was rebound and still bleeds; he can't buckle his own sword belt one-handed and hides it from the captains.
Rickard ordered Marro to mind the command tent and let no one in; Marro left the tent to go to the dice house instead.

thread_changes.body: The Triarch pulled the pickets off the eastern ditch, the company's secret approach; only four people knew. Rickard reached for the key at his neck when he heard.

input.summary: At the horse-lines dice house, Dacey Flint pressed Marro to throw his four stags against a pot of about eight. Ser Tobbin asked Marro whether he had seen his sister Dagna in the river alleys, and Marro did not answer. Vasso, one of Pallo's men in grey, sat beside Marro and offered to make the thirty-stag debt small or nothing in exchange for papers from Rickard's tent. Marro did not throw the dice; the scene ended with both questions hanging.

updates.body: Ser Tobbin has not seen his sister Dagna (tall, wears a red scarf, works the river boats) in six days; she always came to the camp for his coin. He asked Marro if he had seen her; Marro gave no answer, and Tobbin noticed the silence.
Vasso, Pallo's collector, offered Marro to shrink or cancel his thirty-stag debt in exchange for papers from Rickard Snow's tent. Vasso knows Marro can read.
Dacey Flint keeps the bank at the horse-lines dice house; the pot that morning was seven stags and some copper. Flint spoke as if he knew Marro's fingers were broken by someone collecting a debt.
Marro did not throw the dice at the dice house; his oath to Hesse holds for now.

thread_changes.title: Tobbin's sister
thread_changes.body: Ser Tobbin is asking after Dagna, whom Marro killed. He noticed Marro's silence.

thread_changes.title: Vasso's offer
thread_changes.body: Pallo's man will cancel the debt for papers from Rickard's tent. How did he know Marro reads? Flint may be in on it.
Three days and a bit left. Pallo now offers to take papers from Rickard's tent instead of silver.
